description: Commercial treaties between ancient kingdoms helped regulate trade, protect merchants, define access to ports and markets, and stabilize relations between rival powers. Carthage concluded treaties with Rome that restricted where each side could trade and operate in the western Mediterranean, while Greek cities and Hellenistic kingdoms frequently negotiated agreements granting merchants favorable customs, market access, and safe conduct. The Seleucids, Ptolemies, and other successor states also used diplomatic agreements to secure trade routes and the movement of grain, metals, timber, horses, and luxury goods, making commerce an important tool of both diplomacy and state power.
